scenes.title: Prepare and label the session
scenes.narration: Bring your neutral guide and recruitment plan. Check participant fit and access. Label this as rehearsal, planned or an actual permitted conversation. A rehearsal can build skills but provides no customer evidence.

scenes.title: Confirm the opening
scenes.visual: Two adults in a fictional voluntary conversation
scenes.narration: Explain purpose and time, confirm voluntary participation and say they can skip or stop. Permission to talk does not authorise recording. If recording is declined, do not record; only proceed with an agreed note method.

scenes.title: Listen without pitching
scenes.narration: Ask about the last relevant experience. Listen, allow pauses and avoid defending your idea. Ask what happened next or what a word means. Accept that the current approach may work well.

scenes.title: Keep faithful notes
scenes.narration: Record an anonymous account and its context. Mark paraphrases as notes. Only use quotation marks for words actually captured from an authorised source. If uncertain, write unknown instead of reconstructing a quote.

scenes.title: Respect limits and stop
scenes.narration: Respect decline and stop immediately when asked. Avoid unnecessary personal or sensitive details. Put recordings and identifiable notes only in an approved secure system. Do not upload them into this local prototype.

scenes.title: Close and review
scenes.narration: Thank the person, agree any permitted follow-up and review notes promptly. Separate the reported account from your interpretation. Log contradictions and missing details. One conversation does not establish representative demand or future payment.

sections.label: 02 / LEARN
sections.heading: Listen carefully. Record what you actually know.

children: A reported account
is what someone tells you.
A paraphrase
is your summary of that account.
An exact quote
is wording faithfully captured from an authorised source.
An interpretation
is your explanation of what it might mean.
Review your guide and recruitment permissions before starting.
Confirm purpose, time, voluntary choice and separate recording status.
Ask about a recent experience; listen without pitching or defending.
Probe neutrally: “What happened next?” or “What do you mean by that?”
Respect skipped questions and stop requests immediately.
Close, then review notes promptly and label gaps honestly.
Illustrative rehearsal note

Source: fictional role-play. Paraphrase: the participant describes checking two pages to find registration. Interpretation: route visibility may need exploration. This is practice, not customer evidence.
Faithful recording
Do not turn a vague memory into an exact quote. Mark unclear details “unknown.” A polite compliment is not proof of adoption, payment or market demand.

If recording is declined, do not record. Agree whether note-taking is acceptable before proceeding. If participation or notes are not permitted, stop and mark the session pending or cancelled. “Record” in this lesson includes written notes; this prototype has no audio capture or transcription.

Use anonymous summaries only here; keep identities, recordings and identifiable source material in an approved secure system. If no real conversation has occurred, complete a clearly labeled rehearsal without inventing customer findings. Lesson completion records your learning work, not verified interviews.
